user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot fusion be made inductive — scoring each image on its own, without the test-set min-max normalisation of the released code — without losing AUROC, and does this give a threshold that transfers to unseen modalities? The inductive fusion standardises each branch with leave-one-out statistics of the K normal support images (each support's zero-shot map, and its few-shot map against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports, pooled over patches and levels), adds the standardised branches, and pools the fused map with the mean of its top 2% pixels; the threshold is the 95th percentile of the supports' leave-one-out image scores. Primary outcome: image- and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive fusion on every held-out modality and K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the transductive AUROC across random test subsets and at 10% and 50% prevalence. Secondary outcomes: sensitivity, realised specificity, F1 and expected calibration error at the support-derived threshold. We also record whether the few-shot baselines compared in the target paper (APRIL-GAN, WinCLIP) normalise over the test set in their public code, to judge how widely the finding applies.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Region-mass aggregation: scoring images by their strongest coherent anomalous region
SUMMARY: Threshold each image's per-image-normalised fused map at a support-derived pixel level, extract connected regions, and score the image by the best region's mean score weighted by log area, replacing the max-pixel rule.
HYPOTHESIS: Region-mass aggregation reduces false positives at the support-derived threshold by at least 25% relative to max-pixel aggregation on held-out BMAD modalities with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), with image AUROC within 1 point, and its AUROC degrades less than max pooling when 0.1% of pixels are corrupted with random spikes.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: image aggregation (max pixel, mean, top-2% mean, region mass). Region mass: given the per-image fused map F (LOO-Z standardised), threshold at t_pix = 99th percentile of support LOO pixel scores, find 8-connected components, and score each component c as mean(F_c) * log(1 + |c|); image score = max over components (0 if none). Dependent variables: image AUROC, false positives per image at the support threshold, sensitivity for small lesions (lesion area below 1% of the image), and robustness to injected single-pixel noise.
RATIONALE: MVFA's image score for masked datasets is the single maximum of the fused map, so one spurious pixel decides the label; PSMP-CLIP's move from pixel thresholds to region prompts suggests that anomalies should be scored as coherent regions. A region-level aggregation that requires spatial support for a high score is robust to isolated outliers and works per image.
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: after computing the per-image fused map F (LOO-Z as base normalisation), compute t_pix from support LOO maps; mask = F > t_pix; scipy.ndimage.label(mask, structure=ones(3,3)); for each label compute mean(F[label]) and area; score = max(mean * log(1+area)). 2) Robustness test: add spikes to 0.1% of pixels of F with value max(F)+1 before aggregation. 3) Small-lesion subset: test abnormal images with mask area < 1%. 4) Datasets without masks (OCT17, ChestXray, HIS): apply the same rule to the fused det/seg map. 5) No retraining.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: max (MVFA), mean, top-k mean (k in {1%, 2%, 5%}), region mass. Metrics: image AUROC, FP per image and sensitivity at the support threshold, small-lesion sensitivity, AUROC under spike corruption. Falsification: no FP reduction or AUROC loss above 2 points.

Idea B:
TITLE: Empirical p-value fusion across levels and branches (Fisher-MVFA)
SUMMARY: Turn each level/branch patch score into an empirical p-value against support-normal LOO scores and combine them with Fisher's method, giving a per-image, distribution-free anomaly statistic and a principled threshold.
HYPOTHESIS: On held-out BMAD modalities, Fisher p-value fusion matches MVFA's transductive fusion within 1 AUROC point for K >= 4, and its support-derived threshold achieves a realised false-positive rate within 5 points of nominal, whereas a raw-sum per-image fusion without test-set normalisation loses at least 3 AUROC points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: combination rule (raw sum + test-set min-max vs. empirical p-value fusion). For each branch b and level l, the null distribution is the set of LOO patch scores of the K support normals. A test patch score s gets p_bl = (1 + #{null >= s}) / (1 + N_null). The fused pixel statistic is X = -2 * sum_{b,l} log p_bl (Fisher), and the image statistic is the mean of the top 2% pixels of X. Because X is built from tail probabilities, a threshold can be read from the support LOO image statistics. Dependent variables: AUROC (image, pixel), PRO, thresholded sensitivity/specificity/F1, ECE, and per-level contribution analysis.
RATIONALE: MVFA and MLCA add the four levels' raw maps and then min-max them over the test set; levels have different score scales, so the sum is dominated by whichever level has the largest spread. Converting every level and branch score into an empirical tail probability against the support normals puts all evidence on a common, calibrated scale and makes the combination inductive.
METHOD: 1) utils.py: add null_scores(supports) returning, per branch and level, the sorted 1-D array of LOO patch scores (K x 289 values) and empirical_p(s, null) via np.searchsorted. 2) test_few.py: for each test image compute p_bl for all 289 patches at each of 4 levels and 2 branches, X_patch = -2 sum log p (16 x 16-bit floats per patch), bilinearly upsample X to 240x240; image score = mean of top 2%. 3) Ties and extreme scores: p is floored at 1/(1+N_null), so X is bounded. 4) Threshold: 95th percentile of the support LOO image statistics. 5) Variant: weighted Fisher with level weights estimated from the separability of LOO normals vs. the other branch (no target labels). 6) No retraining.
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together), checkpoints of the underlying MVFA model selected on a validation split of the source modalities (never the target test set); MVFA baseline re-run under the same rule; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws (new seed files generated from BMAD valid/ with a fixed RNG); mean and standard deviation reported. Baselines: transductive MVFA fusion; per-image raw sum; LOO-Z (z-score fusion) as a parametric alternative. Ablations: Fisher vs. Stouffer vs. min-p combination; per-level vs. all-level null pools; aggregation operator. Metrics as in the problem. Falsification: AUROC loss above 2 points or realised FPR deviating by more than 10 points from nominal.
